data.name: Highschool Possession
data.detailed_description:
Our protagonist, a fairly ordinary, normal, down to earth young man, has his whole world view shattered when a strange force comes to him and causes him to switch bodies with his classmates. But not just any bodies, he leaps into the bodies of his two 'school idols' the girls he has had a crush on for a long time and been unsure who to ask out.

What initially seems great soon takes a darker turn as he realizes his two 'perfect idols' have some secrets of their own.
What is more he has no idea what is happening to his own body or what is causing this supernatural event.

A casual visual novel to play,
With multiple options to choose,
Featuring two romance options to explore,
In a not so ordinary slice of life adventure.

reviews.review:
[i]Highschool Possession[/i] is first of Dharker Studio's games that I've decided to try, since it's been sitting in my library for quite some time. Reviews are mixed here around in the community about this, due to the game's "mixed" quality altogether. I, personally, am not impressed though. Sure I wasn't expecting anything groundbreaking, but narrative depth, or at least originality is everything for me in a game and it is exactly what the game fails at. Even though it tries to deal with some common and serious emotional problems, [i]Highschool Possession[/i] fails to present any sincerity about the issue.

Well... the story starts a bit generic, as we being the high school student Hikaru who has a crush divided between two ladies: Akiko and Kasumi. Akiko seems to be the good natured and ladylike of the duo, and Kasumi is the silent, submissive yet sporty one who also attends the Swimming Team alongside Hikaru. As we pass through the introductory scene, Hikaru gets a nasty headache and decides to lay down in his room. From there on, we wake up in our lady friends' bodies, switching between them as we wake up each morning. Apparently, we are in a coma and we decide to utilize this supernatural and never properly explained opportunity to learn more about our crushes. As the story progresses, we realize these golden girls do not live golden lives anyhow. Akiko is heavily depressed and enduring an abusive relationship, as Kasumi is constantly bullied at school while her self-confidence gets crippled before the bully. So, we try to better girls' lives by influencing their choices.

Here is the thing: the game can be played either with the NC-17 material or without it. But it's a lose-lose situation concerning this content. Without the adult material patch, there will be some implications within narrative about what happened, yet the plot is heavily undermined. It is more than obvious someone cut out a portion of the story. With the adult patch though... well, brace yourself for some amateur hentai pictures, which really don't fit for the tone of the game, at all.

The story openly discusses that these girls were emotionally abused, so sexualizing them this openly is more of a damage to their psyche and an insult to their character depth – if there is any to begin with. It also undermines the genuineness of their situation. One moment a girl comes into a heartbreaking confession, tears welling up - and the next second she gets feisty and gets ready to be nailed down by the now boyfriend protagonist. I mean, it's not the pornographic part that is disgusting - its target directly cheapens everything, as if artworks are not exaggerated fan service enough. Let us not lie to ourselves, we all are human and bear lust to a degree, so pornography, or at least well done pornography is okay. But when dealing emotional material in a VN - not lustful, EMOTIONAL - bringing in fan service or worse, p0rn, cheapens the context. If you wanna present sexuality, just present it and do it better. Just do no wrap it up with "we are trying to deal with depression here". That's plain lame.

Another side note: If you are familiar with anime/manga culture even the slighest bit, you'll realize that these girls are lamely altered physical copies of Rei and Asuka from [i]Neon Genesis Evangelion[/i]. School uniforms, hair colors and styles, even the fact that one of them is a swimmer are too much of a tell. They could have had original character design, at least.

Art? Not interesting. Music? 2-3 tracks repeating over and over again. Character expressions? Weird and limited. Game time? Really short. Plot? Nope, it is softcore hentai covered under "dealing with depression" flag. I sincerely cannot recommend this one to anyone, for any reason whatsoever. Especially not for 7 dollars. You can get many 1 dollar, or even free VNs with much more depth and sense of emotional community compared to this one. Even if you want some hentai for the spare time, you can do much better.

Please also check out Lady Storyteller's Curator page [url=http://steamcommunity.com/groups/ladystoryteller#curation]here[/url] - follow for regular updates on reviews for other games!
